topology: 2 nodes x4 H100, NVSHMEM put-ring over 8 PEs, both providers in one process
golden: committed (verified, determinism gate: gate runs A/B in job 43964192 plus the independent suite job 43920698 — all three byte-identical)
why: the unified NVLink+IB TRAFFIC timeline: the ring's 6 intra-node hops go over NVLink and its 2 inter-node hops over IB, in ONE execution. This is the capture that makes cross-transport causality recoverable — replay cannot express it, since its passes are different executions.
history: was xfail from 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-28: multinode NVSHMEM hung under NVBit. Root cause was instrumenting LOCAL-memory accesses (per-thread stack / spilled registers) in NVSHMEM's inlined proxy-enqueue path; bisected to a single LDL.64 in nvshmemi_transfer_rma_p<int>. Fixed in 3c5d55f by instrumenting only GLOBAL/GENERIC/GLOBAL_TO_SHARED. The mechanism — why instrumenting a stack reload wedges the proxy handshake — is still unexplained; see things-to-circle-back-to.md.
oracle_note: cross_transport is the point of the case: PE3 and PE7 are the node-crossing senders and record nvlink_accesses=0 while carrying ~196,690 IB sends each; the other six ranks record 196608 NVLink accesses (65536 x 3) and only bootstrap-level IB traffic. That asymmetry is not a defect — inter-node NVSHMEM moves payload by descriptor + NIC, not by GPU loads/stores, so an address tracer cannot see the IB hops at all. Pairing gpumem with ibverbs is what makes the full ring observable.
